chain_trace.break_detail: The DEFECT signal originates from a script-side oracle defect, not from an API behavior deviation (R27 artifact family, variant form). check_common (script lines 279-296) compares every point's vector against a single baseline BASEVEC captured from point 1 only (line 328: bv = m[1].get("vector")), while the seed vectors [float(i), 1.0, 0.5, 0.25] differ per point in direction; on the Cosine collection the stored vector is the L2-normalized raw vector (source: cosine_preprocess, by-design at upsert), and normalization preserves direction, so points 2/3 read back [0.86772,0.43386,0.21693,0.10847] and [0.93420,0.31140,0.15570,0.07785] — differing from BASEVEC by 0.22/0.35, five orders of magnitude above vec_eq's 1e-6 tolerance, at every checkpoint INCLUDING the pre-overwrite baseline. Per the dispatch's R27 decision rule: the log's own pre-overwrite baseline for the only verifiable point (point 1) shows the normalized vector and the post-overwrite readback is byte-identical → R27 artifact family. The script's docstring even cites the R27 lesson ('vector oracles compare readback-vs-baseline-readback only') but implements a single-vector baseline instead of per-point baselines. The contract assertion's own domain (payload replace semantics) was fully satisfied per the log's own OK lines, and the source call chain shows the overwrite path structurally cannot touch vector storage.

Separately, vector L2 normalization happens exactly once at upsert: Segment::upsert_point calls vectors.preprocess (entry.rs:662) → CosineMetric::preprocess → cosine_preprocess (simple.rs:178-232), with the explicit design comment at simple.rs:168 ('Equivalent to DotProductMetric with normalization of the vectors in preprocessing') — on a Cosine collection every stored vector, including points 2/3's differently-directed seeds, is normalized at write and then immutable under payload operations (point 1 byte-identical across three overwrites in the log). The six DEFECT lines are fully explained by the oracle comparing points 2/3 against point 1's baseline vector.
